MODAL_COULD.text: At lunch, Saki saw two green bags on a table. One was hers, but both bags looked almost the same. She first looked for her name, but the labels only showed the letters S.K. and S.M. Then Saki remembered the food card in her bag. Her card had a red circle because she could not eat one kind of nut. She carefully opened only the small outside pocket of the S.K. bag and saw the red card. She knew that bag was hers. She left the S.M. bag closed and told her friend where it was.

PAST_PROGRESSIVE.text: During the lunch break, Kota went to the library and saw wet footprints near a window. A student was standing there with a book, so Kota first thought the student brought water inside. He did not say anything. He looked around and found a yellow cleaning sign behind a shelf. Then he saw a cloth and a small bucket near the window. The librarian came back. She said rain came through the open window that morning. She cleaned most of the floor, but the corner was still wet. The student was only waiting for the floor to dry. Kota was glad. He checked the area first and did not blame anyone. He helped move one chair away from the wet place. Before leaving, Kota noticed that the footprints stopped beside the cloth, not at the student's shoes. That was one more reason to wait for an explanation.

WANT_TO.text: Aya's volleyball team had practice after school. In the gym, she found two new volleyballs beside the wall. They were the same color and size. Aya did not want to use another team's ball. She checked the small number on each ball. One said 14 and the other said 18. Then she looked at the practice chart. Her team had Ball 18 on Tuesday, and another team had Ball 14. Aya took Ball 18 to her team. Later, the other team came and found Ball 14 in the same place. The number and the chart made the choice clear.

PASSIVE.text: Haru's class grew three kinds of plants by the classroom window. On Friday, one name marker fell out of a pot. Haru found the marker on the floor, but the right pot was not clear. He looked at the planting map in the class notebook. The middle pot was marked ‘basil.' Then he compared the leaves with a picture from Monday. The middle plant had the same round leaves as the basil in the picture. Haru put the marker into that pot. He showed the map and the picture to his teacher, and the teacher said his check was careful.

ASK_TELL_WANT_O_TO.text: The teacher asked Riku to give out English worksheets. He found two piles on the teacher's desk. The first pile started on page 32, but the second started on page 34. Both had the same lesson title. Riku almost mixed the piles together. Then he looked at the board. On the board, he saw, ‘Today: pages 32-33. Next class: pages 34-35.' Riku gave his classmates the first pile and left the second pile on the desk. When the teacher arrived, she thanked him for checking. A small page number stopped a simple mistake.

BECAUSE_CLAUSE.text: Mei found a white cap beside the school garden after club time. Three students worked there that day. The cap had no name inside, but it had a small green leaf badge. Mei checked the gardening duty list. Only one of the three students was in the Green Club, and members of that club used the same leaf badge. Mei took the cap to the club room instead of putting it in a random classroom. A student there recognized it and called its owner. Mei was happy because she had used the badge and the duty list together.

MODAL_COULD.text: Toma came to school for a Saturday activity. The classroom clock showed 8:40, but his phone showed 8:30. He thought the clock was broken. Before changing it, he checked the clock in the hall. It also showed 8:40. Then Toma read a note on the activity board. It said, ‘For today's event, the clocks in Rooms 2 and 3 are ten minutes ahead. Please be ready before each group arrives.' The first visitors were coming at 9:00. Toma understood the reason. The clocks were ten minutes fast on purpose, so the student staff could prepare early. He left the clock alone. At 8:50 on his phone, the room clock showed 9:00, and the student staff were already ready at the door. The note also reminded the staff to check their own phones for the real time before opening the doors. That detail showed that the faster clocks were only a preparation tool, not the official event time.

MODAL_MAY_MIGHT.text: Yuna checked the bus list before a class trip. Every student's name was on the list, but Seat 12 was empty. She worried because one student might not have a seat. Then she saw a small note beside Seat 12: ‘Camera box.' The class had a large box for two school cameras, and the teacher did not want it in the aisle. Yuna counted the names again. All thirty students had seats, and Seat 12 was the only place without a name. She told her friend that no student was missing. The empty seat had a job of its own.

BECAUSE_CLAUSE.text: Shun carried old paper to the recycling corner. One box had two arrows on its side. A blue arrow pointed to a narrow opening, and a gray arrow pointed to a larger opening. Shun first thought both openings were for paper. He read the words under the arrows. The blue side said ‘flat paper,' and the gray side said ‘paper cups.' His papers were flat worksheets, so he used the blue opening. A teacher later showed him that cups needed a different process. Shun was glad that he had read the words instead of using the larger opening just because it was easier.

WANT_TO.text: Emi helped prepare a classroom art display. One picture had no name card, and its artist was not clear. Emi did not want to write a name without evidence. She noticed a tiny star in the lower right corner. In an older class folder, she found three pictures with the same star. All three belonged to Ken. She also checked the date on the back of the new picture. It matched Ken's group week for that theme. Emi showed the picture to Ken before she made a new card. Ken smiled and said it was his. He forgot to write his name because the bell rang at the end of class. Emi added the card only after the symbol, the date, and Ken's answer agreed. The teacher then wrote Ken's name in the class record too. Now the picture and the record had the same name.

BECAUSE_CLAUSE.text: Daichi found a key near the shoe boxes after school. The key had a yellow tag with the number 4. He did not try it in nearby doors because he did not know what it opened. Instead, he took it to the staff room. A teacher checked the school key list. Number 4 was the spare key for the art room. The art teacher was still in the building and confirmed that one spare key was missing. Daichi gave the key to the teacher. He was glad. He checked the tag and the list, and he did not test the key himself.

WH_TO_INFINITIVE.text: Mio saw a blue line of tape on the school floor before an open-school event. It started at the front door but did not go toward the usual office. She thought, “Is this line here by mistake?” At the next corner, she found a sign: ‘Visitors: follow the blue line. The main hall is under repair.' Mio followed the line and reached a side entrance to the meeting room. Later, two visitors asked her where to go. She showed them the blue line and the sign. The line looked strange at first, but it was a temporary guide around the repair area.

PAST_PROGRESSIVE.text: Kenta was helping with a small book display in the library. On Wednesday, he saw one display book on the normal shelf. He thought, “Is the display over?” and started to move the other books too. Then he checked the card beside the display. It said the display would continue until Friday. Kenta also looked at the return slip inside the missing book. A student borrowed it before the display began and returned it that morning. Kenta showed the slip to the librarian before he moved the book. She checked the date and said, “The student made a mistake.” The student did not know that the book now belonged on the special table. Kenta told the librarian, and they put the book back on the display. He left the other books where they were. Checking both the event card and the return slip showed him why one book had moved early.

WANT_TO.text: Rina met a visitor near the school entrance. The visitor wanted to find the nurse's room. Rina opened a school map, but two rooms near the center had similar shapes. One had a small star beside it. Rina checked the map legend. The star meant ‘health and first aid.' The other room had a square mark for the office. Rina followed the path from the entrance to the star and walked with the visitor. They reached the nurse's room without going into the office first. The small symbol and the legend made the map clear.
